title: Yellowmoon DevelopSettings
description: The settings of one photo (docs/23 section 3, docs/01 section DevelopSettings): the node-first JSON of the ym:Settings XMP property, of `ym render --settings`, of the golden-image manifest and of the IPC types in src/api/types.ts. A photo's settings are the graph of its nodes; `{}` is the default graph. Every property is optional when reading (a missing one takes its default, shown here); unknown properties are refused, and so is a flat document in the form of Yellowmoon 0.1. Values outside their ranges are clamped by the core, not refused; the ranges here are the ones the core clamps to. Not expressible in JSON Schema and checked by the core: the rules of the graph (exactly one Input, Output and Main; ports and types of links (a mixer's inputs are picture.1 to picture.8, numbered from 1 with no gap; red, green and blue are pictures); one link per input; Main takes its picture from the Input; no circle; at most 64 numbered nodes (correctors, Film nodes, mixers, Splitters and Combiners), 64 masks a node, 100,000 brush points, 256 Object points), colour-balance points lie in the unit disc (a longer vector is scaled back to its circle), colour-warp points lie in the disc of radius 0.5 (likewise), a locked warp pin's target is its source, curve points are sorted by x with no two at the same x (a curve is sorted when read), a crop rectangle lies in the unit square (it is moved or shrunk to fit), and Auto reads as a manual 0 in every corrector but Main.

nodes.description: The graph of the photo: its nodes and the links between them. Left out, `nodes` is the default graph: Input → 1 Main → Output with every field at its default.

items.description: The nodes, in no particular order when read (written Input, numbered nodes by id, Output). The Input and the Output are items like the others and cannot be added to or taken out; at most 64 numbered nodes together (correctors, Film nodes, Face Refinement nodes, mixers, Splitters and Combiners), Main included.

links.description: The links. Left out, the default links (Input → Main → Output); given, they replace the default links whole. An input has one link, so at most 64 × 8 + 1 = 513.

input_node.description: The Input (`docs/23` section 3.2): the raw, light and framing settings. Every property but `id` is optional when reading and takes its default; the fixed three nodes need not be listed.

white_pick.description: Pick white: [x, y] in [0, 1]^2 on the photo as the camera oriented it, or null.

rolloff.description: RAW > Range, each 0 to 1 (docs/02 C7). The name is kept from the earlier roll-off card.

highlights.description: The highlight range: where the camera's clipping point lands, from where it was recorded (0) to white, the clip of an ALEXA at EI 800 (1). Mid grey and everything under the knee, two stops below the camera's clip, never move. A document without this field reads as 0.6; an explicit value is kept.

low_light.description: The low-light toe: softens the noise near black (0 is off).

decode.description: RAW > Decode switches; all true by default.

crop.description: The crop, or null for none.

auto.description: The crop is Auto crop's proposal (docs/20-auto-crop.md section 2); absent is false. Rendering never reads it.

orientation.description: Rotation after the camera's EXIF orientation, in degrees clockwise. Any multiple of 90 is read and normalised.

output_node.description: The Output: the look and the sharpening at the size the picture is shown or written.

look.description: Look id: builtin:<slug>, user:<slug>, arri:<group number>:<slug> or arri-display:<input>:<target>. A document without `look` is read as the user's default look (builtin:signature out of the box) by a session and by `ym render`; the blank value, shown as the default here, is builtin:neutral.

output_sharpening.description: Detail > Sharpening > Output: the strength of the sharpening applied to the picture at the size it is shown or written, in percent (0 is off). A plain number, not Auto; the UI steps by 5. A document without it reads as 100.

corrector_node.description: A corrector node, Main (id 1) included. A node with an id the default graph does not have must give its `kind`.

id.description: A corrector's id: an integer 1 to 2147483647 (Main is 1). Ids are unique within the photo.

name.description: 1 to 32 characters after trimming; a longer name is cut and an empty one reads as the default ("Main" for node 1, "Corrector").

film_node.description: A Film node (docs/24): a colour negative, an enlarger, a print and a scan. A node with an id the default graph does not have must give its `kind`. The stock and the paper are profile ids of data/film/ (`ym film list`); a stock or paper that is not there is refused.

id.description: A numbered node's id: an integer 2 to 2147483647. Ids are unique within the photo, correctors and Film nodes together.

name.description: 1 to 32 characters after trimming; a longer name is cut and an empty one reads as the default ("Film").

stock.description: The profile id of a camera film.

paper.description: The profile id of a paper; null is the stock's matching paper. A slide takes none (it reads as null).

seed.description: Not in the interface; it keeps the grain a function of the settings.

strength.description: Percent: how much of the film look is applied.

face_refinement_node.description: A Face Refinement node (docs/27): retouches the faces it finds (found automatically, numbered from 1, left to right) with Blemish, Dark circles, Even skin and Texture, Skin grading and Teeth whitening, leaving the painted `protect` areas alone. A node with an id the default graph does not have must give its `kind`. Until the render step lands (S-11b) the node passes its picture through unchanged.

id.description: A numbered node's id: an integer 2 to 2147483647. Ids are unique within the photo, correctors, Film nodes, Face Refinement nodes and mixers together.

name.description: 1 to 32 characters after trimming; a longer name is cut and an empty one reads as the default ("Face Refinement").

same_for_all.description: "Same for all faces": when true, `all` serves every face and `faces` is kept but not used.

all.description: The amounts every face takes while `same_for_all` is true, and when `faces` is empty.

faces.description: The amounts per face; entry n is face n + 1, numbered from 1, left to right. At most 32. A face past the end of the list takes face 1's amounts.

protect.description: The protection plane: strokes painted on the photo, in the format of a Brush mask row (without its row fields). Painted areas are left alone by every tool; at most 100,000 points in all.

face_settings.description: The amounts of the Face Refinement tools for one face (docs/27 section 3). A left-out amount takes its default: Blemish 30, Dark circles 30, Even skin 25, everything else 0.

texture.description: Texture; 0 keeps the skin's fine detail as it is.

pos.description: The card's place on the canvas: [x, y] in grid units, finite numbers in -1000 to 1000 (the core clamps). Left out, the core places the nodes in a row by their number (the Input at -1, the correctors from 0, the Output last), at y = 0.

trim.description: A corrector's trims (`docs/algorithms/06` section 2): an exposure trim in stops and a temperature and tint trim.

grade.description: A corrector's grade: the fields the settings had before they were nodes. Auto belongs to Main (id 1): in any other corrector Auto reads as a manual 0 and is written as one.

color_balance.description: Three wheels. Shadows and highlights are Auto ([0, 0], or the colour Apple Auto gave that zone, docs/19 section 5) or a manual point; midtones is a point [a, b] in the unit disc.

color_warp.description: Colour > Colour warp (docs/02 C9b): pins that move chosen colours across the chroma plane, in order. At most 16 (the core cuts the rest). No pins by default, which skips the stage. A patch replaces the whole list.

curve.description: Luma, red, green and blue curves, 2 to 16 control points each.

masks.description: A corrector's masks: its Invert and up to 64 rows that add up (`docs/23` section 3.3).

mask.description: One mask row: `kind` and the fields common to every row (mode, invert, enabled, opacity), then the kind's own.

mask_object.description: Object (SAM 2.1 from clicks or a box): `points` are [x, y, positive] in the photo frame, at most 256; with no point and no box it selects nothing.

box.description: [x0, y0, x1, y1] in the photo frame, or null.

mask_subject.description: Subject (Apple Vision's foreground; a Mac that supports it).

mask_people.description: People (Apple Vision's people; a Mac that supports it).

mask_background.description: Background (the blur map with a level and a softness).

mask_linear.description: Linear: a line through `center` at `angle_deg` with a feather.

mask_radial.description: Radial: an ellipse with radii in fractions of the long edge.

mask_brush.description: Brush: strokes drawn into a raster; at most 100,000 points in all.

mask_color_range.description: Colour range: a centre in the chroma plane of C9 (at most 0.5 long), a width and a softness.

mask_brightness_range.description: Brightness range: low, high and a softness. A `low` above `high` is read as both at their mean.

link.description: A link from an output port to an input port of the same type, picture to picture or key to key. An input has at most one link; the Output's picture is linked once; Main takes its picture from the Input; the links make no circle (`docs/23` section 3.5).

port.description: A port name. A corrector or Film node has `picture` and `key`; a Parallel or Layer has the inputs `picture.1` to `picture.8` (numbered from 1 with no gap) and the output `picture`; a Splitter has the input `picture` and the outputs `red`, `green` and `blue`; a Combiner has the inputs `red`, `green` and `blue` and the output `picture`. Which node has which port is checked by the core (docs/25 section 2.2).

lens.description: Look > Lens (docs/21 section 2): the lens and how much of its character each slider brings. All three amounts at 0 is no lens, whatever `kind` says. Choosing a lens does not move the amounts by itself: the card and `ym render --lens` send the lens's starting amounts (`ym lenses list`) with it. A patch may carry only the parts it changes.

flares.description: Glow around bright light, veiling glare, ghosts and starbursts (L3).

edges.description: Edge softness and darkening, colour fringes and the lens's distortion (L2, L4).

anamorphic.description: An anamorphic attachment in front of the lens: taller bokeh that takes the lens's own swirl and cat's-eye shapes, horizontal streaks, the anamorphic bend (L1 to L4).

auto_percent.description: contrast, highlights, shadows, black and saturation: Auto (0, or Apple Auto's value for the photo, docs/19 section 5), or a manual value from -100 to 100 (the UI steps by 1). A plain number is an older document: it reads as Manual with that value, and 0 as Auto.

exposure.description: Auto, or an absolute exposure in stops (the UI steps by 0.01).

white_balance.description: Auto, or Kelvin and tint (the UI steps Kelvin by 50; positive tint is magenta).

sharpen.description: Auto, or an amount and a radius in pixels.

noise_reduction.description: Auto, or luminance, colour and detail strengths.

auto_disc_point.description: The shadows or highlights wheel: Auto ([0, 0], or Apple Auto's colour for that zone, docs/19 section 5), or a manual point. A plain point is an older document: it reads as Manual at that point, and [0, 0] as Auto.

disc_point.description: [a, b] with a^2 + b^2 <= 1 (the core scales a longer vector back to the circle).

warp_pin.description: One pin of the colour warp: the colours near `source` move to `target`. Every property but `source` may be left out and takes the default shown (`target`: the source). A locked pin holds the colours within its range in place; its target is its source and its weights, pivot, exposure and saturation are the defaults.

chroma_point.description: [a, b] on the chroma plane of the colour warp (a: red against cyan, b: green against blue) with a^2 + b^2 <= 0.25 (the core scales a longer vector back to |c| = 0.5).

curve.description: 2 to 16 control points [x, y] in [0, 1]^2, x strictly increasing. Default: the identity [[0, 0], [1, 1]].

parallel_node.description: A Parallel mixer (docs/25 section 3.2): adds the change each of its inputs makes to the picture they started from, on LogC4 code values. It has the inputs picture.1 to picture.N (N at most 8) and the output picture, no masks and no controls. A bypassed Parallel outputs its base.

id.description: A numbered node's id: an integer 2 to 2147483647. Ids are unique within the photo, correctors, Film nodes and these nodes together.

name.description: 1 to 32 characters after trimming; a longer name is cut and an empty one reads as the default ("Parallel").

layer_node.description: A Layer mixer (docs/25 section 3.3): stacks its inputs, input 1 at the bottom, and blends each over the ones below it in linear light, through the mask of the node that feeds it times `opacity`. It has the inputs picture.1 to picture.N (N at most 8) and the output picture, and no masks. A bypassed Layer outputs input 1.

id.description: A numbered node's id: an integer 2 to 2147483647. Ids are unique within the photo, correctors, Film nodes and these nodes together.

name.description: 1 to 32 characters after trimming; a longer name is cut and an empty one reads as the default ("Layer").

mode.description: How a layer blends over the ones below it.

opacity.description: 0 to 1; a value outside is clamped.

splitter_node.description: A Splitter (docs/25 section 3.4): sends the red, green and blue of its `picture` input to the outputs `red`, `green` and `blue`, each a grey picture of one channel. No masks, no Bypass.

id.description: A numbered node's id: an integer 2 to 2147483647. Ids are unique within the photo, correctors, Film nodes and these nodes together.

name.description: 1 to 32 characters after trimming; a longer name is cut and an empty one reads as the default ("Splitter").

combiner_node.description: A Combiner (docs/25 section 3.4): joins the pictures on its inputs `red`, `green` and `blue` into one picture, a channel from each. No masks, no Bypass.

id.description: A numbered node's id: an integer 2 to 2147483647. Ids are unique within the photo, correctors, Film nodes and these nodes together.

name.description: 1 to 32 characters after trimming; a longer name is cut and an empty one reads as the default ("Combiner").
